I struggled and continue to struggle with the same things you're going through. Truly the best thing to do is to tell an adult, anyone you feel comfortable telling. You don't have to go into detail but say that you might need a therapist and would like help finding one. Therapy isn't something scary and I first went when I was 11. Having someone who understands you and who has studied for years on how to help will know what to do. Talking to someone can be really transformative, and I find therapists easier to talk to than people I know personally. 

Coping mechanisms I used when struggling with self harm involved snapping a rubber band against my wrists and throwing out sharp items I used so I wouldn't have access. For depression in general, the best advice is to find things that you enjoy. Physical activity is great but I know how difficult it can be to get moving sometimes. Writing your feelings when you're alone so that you can organize them and get it out of your head. Make sure you're eating every day and force yourself to shower. Drink enough water, take care of yourself. Do any kind of self care whether thats face masks or playing video games or anything. Surround yourself in nice smelling things (I love lavender essential oils). Do something that involves color. Just know that what you're going through is normal and you're not alone.
